title_en: Liao Changyi v. Liao Lunwan — dispute over real estate
keywords_en: Civil; Real estate dispute; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; Natural person; Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation); Ownership of house property; Determination of joint purchase of house; Validity of title deed; Reversal; House sale; Property registration; Co-ownership dispute; Real estate dispute between Liao Changyi and Liao Lunwan
full_text_en:
Liao Changyi v. Liao Lunwan — dispute over house property

Petitioner: Liao Changyi, male, 70 years old, from Xinyi County, Guangdong Province, overseas Chinese. Currently residing in Bahau, Malaysia.

Agent ad litem: Liao Shifeng (son of Liao Changyi), male, 42 years old, currently residing in Hong Kong.

Respondent: Liao Lunwan, male, 68 years old, from Xinyi County, Guangdong Province. Currently residing in Xincheng Town, Xinyi County.

In 1973, the Petitioner Liao Changyi sent a letter authorizing his son Liao Shifeng, who was in China, to apply to the government for approval to purchase a house. At the same time, the Respondent Liao Lunwan also wanted to buy a house. Through the introduction of Li Rirong, Liao Shifeng and Liao Lunwan negotiated the purchase of a house owned by Liang Shiyong and Liang Shihui, located at No. 99, Yanjiang First Road, Xincheng Town, Xinyi County. The parties agreed on a purchase price of RMB 4,300. On January 21, 1974, Liao Shifeng and Liao Lunwan each paid RMB 2,000 to the seller, leaving an outstanding balance of RMB 300. On the same day, Liao Lunwan's son, Liao Changya, filled out the draft deed, which included only the name of Liao Changyi and not the name of Liao Lunwan. The seller noted on the previous deed: "This house belongs to Liao Changyi." After Liao Shifeng completed the tax deed and the formal deed, he moved into the house in May 1974. Shortly thereafter, Liao Lunwan claimed an interest in the property, asserting that he had contributed RMB 2,000 and that it had been agreed with Liao Shifeng that the deed would be in Liao Changyi's name, but that they were in fact co-purchasers of the house. Liao Shifeng acknowledged that Liao Lunwan had paid RMB 2,000 but denied any agreement to use Liao Changyi's name on the deed, claiming instead that Liao Lunwan had withdrawn from the purchase. Therefore, the buyer on the tax deed and the owner on the formal deed was Liao Changyi, and the house should belong to Liao Changyi. A dispute arose between the parties. On June 11, 1976, Liao Lunwan forcibly moved into the disputed house, escalating the conflict. After multiple failed mediations by the local government and the Xinyi County People's Court, the County People's Court transferred the case to the Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court for trial at first instance in June 1980.

The Zhanjiang Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held that the accounts of Liao Lunwan and Liao Shifeng differed, but based on all the deeds and certificates, the property right should belong to Liao Changyi. On October 30, 1980, it ruled that the house belonged to Liao Changyi, and that Liao Changyi should return RMB 2,000 plus interest to Liao Lunwan. Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Liao Lunwan appealed.

The Guangdong High People's Court, after trial, held that the case could not be decided solely on the deeds and certificates; Liao Lunwan had contributed money and participated in the house purchase, and the fact of joint purchase should be recognized. On October 7, 1981, it modified the judgment, ruling that the disputed house was jointly owned by Liao Changyi and Liao Lunwan, each holding a half share. Dissatisfied with the final judgment, Liao Changyi petitioned the Supreme People's Court for a retrial, requesting that the house be awarded to him.

The Civil Division of the Supreme People's Court, after reviewing the case files and conducting on-site investigations, held that China has a tax deed system, and that the transfer of ownership of immovable property must be based on the tax deed. The legally recognized deed approved by the government for the sale of a house is the primary basis for determining property rights. With respect to the house disputed between Liao Changyi and Liao Lunwan, although Liao Lunwan initially intended to jointly purchase the house with Liao Changyi and paid part of the purchase price, when the formal procedures for the transfer of property rights were carried out, he did not participate in the registration or exercise his right to purchase. This should be regarded as an automatic waiver. Liao Lunwan's claim that the use of Liao Changyi's name on the deed was agreed upon with Liao Shifeng is not established due to lack of evidence and Liao Shifeng's denial. Therefore, it is not recognized. Liao Changyi authorized Liao Shifeng to purchase the house, completed the legal procedures, and obtained a lawful deed, which should be protected by law. However, his failure to promptly return the RMB 2,000 to Liao Lunwan or submit it to the court for disposition was improper. Additionally, Liao Changyi still owes Liang Shiyong and Liang Shihui RMB 300 for the house purchase, which should also be settled together.

Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to the trial supervision procedure under Chapter 14 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), and after discussion by the Judicial Committee, decided to retry the case. After trial, on December 28, 1984, it rendered the following judgment: The final judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court is reversed; the property right of the house belongs to Liao Changyi; Liao Changyi shall repay Liao Lunwan RMB 2,000 plus interest of RMB 947.64; Liao Changyi shall pay an additional RMB 300 plus interest of RMB 142.15 to Liang Shiyong and Liang Shihui for the house purchase; Liao Lunwan is ordered to vacate the house within six months from the date this judgment takes effect.
